paras: The shooting of Frank Wiley was the wounding of a Black man by Marshal Flanagan, the town marshal of Metropolis, Illinois, on or about August 16, 1903. Wiley was described as "seriously wounded," and the marshal was reported to have been "fully exonerated" on the claim that Wiley had been trying to assault him. The only known report is a short item in the Paducah Sun of Kentucky, which headlined it as a shooting in self-defense.

According to the Paducah Sun of August 17, Marshal Flanagan shot and seriously wounded Frank Wiley, identified as "colored," in Metropolis the day before. The paper gave no account of where or how the encounter began, what weapon was used, or whether Wiley was under arrest. Its only explanation, attributed to unnamed "reports," was that Wiley had been trying to assault the officer.

The same item stated that the marshal was "fully exonerated," without saying by whom or through what proceeding. The coverage does not show whether Wiley survived his wounds or was charged with any offense.

The Paducah Sun ran the story on page five under the headline "SHOT IN SELF DEFENSE" and the subhead "FRANK WILEY PLUGGED BY MARSHAL FLANAGAN AT METROPOLIS." The headline stated the marshal's justification as fact, while the body hedged it with "according to reports" and referred to Wiley as "The negro." No other white paper and no Black paper is known to have reported the shooting.
